testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.
The brakes may become too smooth to work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in very wet weather when temperatures are below freezing. The brakes can freeze in place and prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their brake systems.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rainwater to enter air tanks.
Remove water and oil from air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil from the system. Water and oil buildup can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system has a leak:

options.text: Both systems will always have leaks.
The other system may still work.
You do not need to worry.
The other system will also fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other system may still work.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: Brake fading happens when:

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough.

questions.explanation: Using brakes too much causes them to overheat and become less effective. This loss of braking power is called fading.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake system, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters. This twists the brake camshafts.

questions.question: The ____ shows how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. It tells the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rainwater to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil buildup can damage the brakes if left in the system.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, a yellow diamond-shaped knob controls the parking brake. Pull it out to engage the parking brake and push it in to release it.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: If brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat, what happens?

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The air compressor will kick on to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: When brakes get too hot from overuse, they expand and change chemically. This makes them less effective and can cause them to stop working. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: What are air brakes?

options.text: An effective tool for stopping large vehicles.
A tool to improve fuel efficiency.

questions.correctAnswerText: An effective tool for stopping large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Cannot be used with air brakes.
Should be used only on dry pavement.
Can help you stay in control when braking.
Should only be used if all axles have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air braking systems. ABS helps you control your vehicle and stops wheels from locking during hard braking on slippery surfaces. ABS helps even if it is on only one axle.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Lift the brake pedal toward you.

questions.explanation: To stop an air-braked vehicle, push the brake pedal down. Control the pressure to stop the vehicle smoothly and safely.

questions.question: A vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to warn that the system is not working properly.
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lamps are usually yellow. Even if ABS is not working, you will still have regular brakes to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, what condition should the air compressor drive belt be in before each drive?
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive on a vehicle with air brakes. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). All other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: What must happen before a vehicle with dual air brakes can operate properly?

options.text: Air pressure stays in the braking system when the vehicle is off.
Some air pressure stays in the braking system when the vehicle is off.
The vehicle must run to build air pressure so the brakes work.
Air pressure stays when shut off for less than four hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must run to build air pressure so the brakes work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, run the engine to build up at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: What happens in a dual air brake system if one system loses pressure?

options.text: Air from the other system will help fill the low pressure system.
The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
The low system will use a backup system to refill the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes may fail. Stop your vehicle safely and have the air system repaired.

questions.question: When is a tank endorsement required?

options.text: When transporting both liquids and gases.
It is optional when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: When transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to transport liquids or gases, with few exceptions. This applies to hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop the vehicle are found inside the drum brake.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Clean the air in the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil buildup can damage the brakes. Use manual drains every day.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Never use the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.
